desc: Read input values for N, M, start position, house locations, and the sequence of moves.
Store house coordinates in a list and create a sorted version of this list optimized for binary searching based on the current move direction (Y-axis for horizontal moves, X-axis for vertical moves).
Initialize the current position $(x, y)$ to $(S_x, S_y)$ and an empty set to track visited house indices.
Update the current position based on the direction and distance.
Define the segment boundaries (min/max x or y) for the current move.
Use binary search on the pre-sorted house list to identify candidate houses that lie on the line of movement.
Iterate through these candidates to check if they fall strictly within the segment range and add their indices to the visited set if they do.
After processing all moves, calculate the total number of unique houses in the visited set.
Print the final coordinates and the count of distinct houses.
Implement the Segment Tree approach to efficiently skip visited houses and avoid $O(NM)$ worst-case scenarios.
Test with provided sample inputs to verify correctness.
